actions.reason:
I found no change to decode_ir that I expect to reach the 1% minimum, so I stopped without editing. I made no edits and ran no evaluations.

What I found:
- Regex is already imported lazily, and load results are cached, so decode pays very little fixed library cost.
- Cache hits happen in 11 of the 12 bench rounds. Their vocab-equality check runs over about 769 entries, which I estimate at around 1M instructions out of about 522M. I had expected about 1.5% from this check. It is negligible, so I left it alone.
- The only real per-element library work left is three first-call list comprehensions of 100k ids each, followed by a C join and a UTF-8 decode.
- The `idx >= 0` branch in that comprehension costs roughly as much as any C-level way to check for negative ids. Earlier sandbox runs measured the `min(ids)` guard, `map` and `itemgetter` variants as worse, by 2.9%, 10.9% and 3.2%.
- I cannot drop the bounds check by padding the list, because a negative id far enough below zero would silently decode to a real token.
- A dict-based lookup would avoid the branch, but the int-key hashing and comparison would likely cost more per id than the branch saves. I did not measure this.

Without a different algorithm for the decode itself, the remaining library cost is too small for a 1% gain on this metric.

journal.text:
I read minbpe/regex.py, minbpe/base.py, minbpe/basic.py and lineage_bench.py, looking for a change to decode_ir. I searched for the decode path, _decode_cache, the vocab equality check and module-level imports and compiles.

I made no edits and ran no evaluations. There is no candidate. I stopped because I found no change I expect to reach the 1% minimum. Regex is already imported lazily. Load results are already cached. So decode pays very little fixed library cost. Cache hits happen in 11 of the 12 bench rounds. On each hit a vocab equality check runs over about 769 entries.

I now believe the fixed costs in decode are already mostly removed. What remains per round is small, and the equality check on cache hits is the only part I found that clearly repeats.

Next I would measure that equality check directly before changing it. One option is to key the cache on vocab identity or a stored hash instead of comparing all entries. If the measured share is under 1%, I should leave decode alone and look elsewhere.
